the study of NK cells in the liver.
the cytotoxicity and cytokine production of HI NK cells and their potential use for immunotherapy.
the cytotoxicity and phenotype of hepatic intrasinusoid (HI) CD56bright natural killer (NK), which has been isolated from human liver perfusate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HI NK cells are effective against HCC cells, but the cytotoxicity is dependent on the type of HCC cells.
HI CD56+ NK cells can be used to screen for HCC cells that would be most responsive to NK cell immunotherapy.
the cytotoxicity against hepatocellular carcinoma cells by intrasinusoidal NK cells is dependent on the expression of TRAIL and FASL, but not on PD-L1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HI NK cells can be used for cancer immunotherapy, and prescreening HCC cells would help identify the most suitable recipients for NK cell therapy.
we identified a subset of NK cells from liver that can kill HCC cells, and we found that the cytotoxicity was mediated through NKG2D and its ligands.
we have identified a novel population of NK cells, which is intrinsically cytotoxic to HCC cells, and we have also demonstrated the mechanisms by which these NK cells exert their cytotoxic activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intrasinusoidal CD56bright natural killer cells are a promising cell source for adoptive immunotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma.
HI CD56dim NK cells are not effective in killing HCC cells, but HI CD56bright cells are effective in killing Huh7 and SNU398 HCC cells.
HI NK cells have the potential to be used for HCC immunotherapy.
